items.gist: Introduces kalādhvā and debates whether kalā is a subtle śakti, convention, or non-ultimate category.
Explains aṇḍa as the cause of world-division and addresses how covering arises despite non-obstruction.
Presents the tattva scheme from earth to Śiva and the higher paraśiva levels.
Moves from meya to mātṛ and describes mantra, pada, and varṇa as levels of the mantric path.
Shows how varṇas express pramā and how speech and convention arise from consciousness.
Describes purification of the sixfold self through mantra and progressive refinement.
Classifies mantras as purifying and explains their graded efficacy in the adhva.
Compares world-appearance to reflection and denies independent external objects.
Uses dream analogy to show that bodies and worlds are consciousness-made appearances.
Identifies Śakti/Śiva as the real support and ground of all apparent bhāvas.
Rejects creation in fixed space and time, affirming consciousness as the sole reality.
Concludes the detailed exposition of kalādhvā and the adhva system.
